newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Packager Van Leer plans multiple takeovers.
newsitem.headline: Packager Van Leer plans multiple takeovers.

text.p: Dutch packager Van Leer said on Tuesday it was planning several acquisitions to expand its consumer packaging business, including a major U.S. buy.
"We have many irons in the fire, but unfortunately nothing has yet been rounded off," Van Leer's chairman Willem de Vlugt told a news conference on the company's first-half results.
The industrial and consumer packaging maker earlier reported first-half net profits available to ordinary shareholders jumped 20.3 percent to 45.3 million from a year-earlier 37.7 million.
De Vlugt said Van Leer was looking at the opportunities for a major U.S acquisition in the disposable tableware sector.
"We're looking for a takeover price of around 60 million guilders," he said.

Van Leer, which was floated on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange last May, was also eyeing takeovers in consumer packaging in eastern Europe, De Vlugt said. The company already owns a tubs and lids producer in Poland.
The company was looking to set up a joint venture in China in the longer term.
"China's noodle market offers fantastic possibilities and we would love to get a hold on that," De Vlugt said. Van Leer already operates a small Chinese plant in Ningbo, near Shanghai.
In the medium-term, the company was seeking to develop the European market for premium disposable tableware.
This was highly profitable in the United States, where Van Leer manufactures high-grade disposable crockery and cutlery for the fast food industry under its Chinet brand.
"We want to achieve a similar position in consumer packaging as we have in industrial packaging," De Vlugt said.
Van Leer is a world leader in industrial packaging (steel drums and drum closures for the oil and chemicals industries) and the sixth-largest player on the European packaging market.

First half acquisitions included loss-making tubs and lids producer Plastona in the United Kingdom and moulded fibre manufacturer Smorgons of Australia. The firm also expanded its Polish tubs and lids activities.
De Vlugt said the takeovers had boosted operating costs. Together with Isea of Italy, another relatively new acquisition, the newcomers had cost 26 million guilders.
"Plastona, which was heavily loss-making when we bought it in April, is now breaking even," De Vlugt said, adding the firm would be contributing to profits by next year.
-- Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
